title: Grateful Dead Live at Roscoe Maples Pavilion, Stanford U. on 1973-02-09

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1973 debut‑song marathon – smoking China>Rider, TLEO, first‑ever Eyes of the World and Here Comes Sunshine.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crystal‑clear soundboard tape with superb instrument separation and a punchy drum mix, only marred by occasional early‑set drop‑outs. Musically the show is a landmark “first‑time” performance packed with raw energy – China>Rider, TLEO, Eyes of the World, Here Comes Sunshine, Row Jimmy, Loose Lucy and many more fire‑cracker rockers make it one of ’73’s most celebrated nights.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews praise both the stellar soundboard quality and the historic, high‑energy performance; only minor technical glitches are noted, resulting in a top‑tier rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with excellent instrument separation and vocal clarity; drum and bass drum punch highlighted. A few reviewers note early‑set drop‑outs or slight muddiness in the first half, but overall the tape is considered one of the best‑sounding SBD sources.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A historic ‘first‑time’ marathon – the first set is a bit rough but packed with debuts; the second set tightens up and delivers nonstop fire, showcasing the band’s evolving groove.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for soaring guitar tone (often high in the mix), creative solos and a blazing intro; described as ‘brilliant’ and ‘very creative’.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted for its clarity and tightness, especially on I Know Your Rider; generally lauded though one reviewer missed his presence later due to mixing.
band_member_comments.Bob: Right‑on rhythm guitar work, lyrical chord voicings and solid vocal harmonies; highlighted as ‘right on’ throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards are praised when audible (especially in Playing in the Band) but several reviewers note he gets lost in the mix for much of the concert.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum mix is singled out as a strength – punchy bass‑drum drive and tight snare; Bill/Mickey’s playing described as energetic and ‘tight’.
